messages:
jorge: heads-up, ran an nsys trace on the staging serving node and hit a weird CUPTI init race when attaching to the running pod. trace aborted, nvtx markers incomplete.

jorge: command was: `nsys profile --output /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite --attach 12345` and got: `CUPTI ERROR: CUPTI_ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION during cuptiActivitySubscribe` then `nsys: failed to attach to process 12345 (CUPTI init failure)`.

alex_m: ugh. which driver + cuda on that node? we've seen CUPTI version mismatches cause that.

mina: node-12: nvidia-driver 535.113, CUDA 12.3, container image uses libcuda from 535.101 (host mounted). i reproduced locally with same combo and got the same subscribe error.

sam: did you try running nsys as root inside container (or using --allow-root)? sometimes rootless attach loses permissions for CUPTI ioctl.

jorge: tried both `--allow-root` and host root; still reproducible. interestingly, when it fails the runtime falls back to software kernel-selection path and we see a ~1.8x token latency regression for long sequences.

mina: timeline snapshot (when it did succeed on a patched node): kernels look normal, but on failed-attach runs the deviceSynchronize and kernel-launch latency explodes. KV cache hit rate drops ~25% (more cache misses), probably because some async prefetch path is disabled when CUPTI hooks fail.

alex_m: can you paste the small perf numbers? helps scope whether kernel selection heuristics or KV cache warmup is the main cost.

jorge: micro-benchmark: 1) baseline (no nsys attach): p50=28ms, p95=62ms; 2) attach-fail case: p50=50ms, p95=110ms. CPU side shows more host wait time, and nvprof shows repeated small kernels instead of fused kernels (looks like an optimization demotion).

sam: hmm that demotion to smaller kernels smells like a kernel-selection fallback where the runtime detects an incompatible tool and picks safe (slower) kernels to avoid unsupported fast paths. could be a CUPTI API quirk that causes our kernel probe to fail and fallback to conservative codegen.

mina: also saw this warning in dmesg: `nvidia: firmware version mismatch, ioctl failed` around the time of attach. ops-bot rolled a node upgrade yesterday evening.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: node-upgrade/nightly applied to k8s-staging pool at 2025-11-06T03:40Z (driver bump 535.101 -> 535.113).

alex_m: ok, likely a driver/CUPTI ABI shift between those micro-versions. quick workaround: use `nsys profile --capture=none --sample=cpu` to get host-side traces and run `nvprof --legacy-api` on a dedicated test job (not attach) to exercise kernels. attaching to busy serving processes is flaky across driver versions.

jorge: plan: 1) reproduce on a dedicated test job with exact image+driver and collect perfetto system trace + nvprof to capture kernel timeline, 2) run a small binary that exercises KV cache hotpath with instrumentation to confirm cache miss spike, 3) open bug with NVIDIA and pin-driver for staging until fixed.

mina: i ran a quick perfetto capture earlier (when attach succeeded) and exported a kernel timeline — attached the svg to the ticket. hotspot was `atten_fused_kernel` on sm_86; when demoted it becomes `atten_block_kernel_small` with extra memcpy/host-syncs.

sam: in the meantime, add a runtime guard to detect CUPTI attach failures and avoid switching to the safe kernel selection (force the previously-known-good kernel) until we have a proper mitigation. that should avoid the 2x perf cliff.

jorge: thanks. i'm going to open a short PR for the conservative guard + a repro job YAML and link the nvprof/perfetto artifacts in the ticket. will also ping nvidia support with the logs + timestamps.

alex_m: ping me on the PR, i'll help with the repro infra (we should test across 535.100 -> 535.115 matrix).

mina: noted. saving the nvprof stdout and a minimal reproducer here: `git@git:/infra/trace-repros/nsys-attach-race`.

sam: one more note — if you need a low-friction trace for hotpath identification, `nsys profile --output /tmp/quick --trace=cuda --force-overwrite --capture-range=all --child-attach-mode=none` on a short dedicated job usually avoids attach races.

jorge: copying this thread into the bug report. I'll update when NVIDIA responds or when we have a pinned-driver rollout plan.
